audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer attributes the reflect to Mel's ULTIMATE in eight places — whys[4], whys[5], whys[6], spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text, content.mid, content.late and wants.foe[1] all say "her R reflect". The reflect is Rebuttal, her W. Golden Eclipse (R) is a 25000-range global that strikes everything carrying Overwhelm stacks and reflects nothing. The full layer has it right, so the page currently contradicts itself. Two further errors ride on top: Rebuttal also prevents her from taking damage at all (not just reflecting), and of Lillia's kit only Swirlseed (E) is a projectile — Watch Out! Eep! cannot be reflected, so "reflect your W slam" is wrong even after the slot is fixed.
audit.why: A player told to fear her ultimate will happily walk into the 38-second W and hold back for a cooldown that does something completely different. The mirror mel__lillia found the reciprocal slot errors in this same pairing.
audit.corrected: All eight strings re-attributed to Rebuttal (W), with the 38s rank-1 / 26s rank-5 cooldown attached and the Swirlseed-only reflect stated in dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.
sources: enemyKit W text "forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles", cd "38/35/33/29/26"
enemyKit R text "strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance"
ownerKit E flag projectile (only ability so flagged)

audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagree with packet.levelChart and with their own whys. Page: Skill/Skill/Skill/Lillia/Lillia/Lillia/Skill. Packet: Mel/Skill/Lillia/Lillia/Skill/Skill/Mel. whys[0] says "concede the level", whys[2] says she pays HP every time she walks up, whys[4] says "even unless your jungler is there", whys[5] literally ends in the word "Skill", whys[6] opens "Mel out-scales".
audit.why: whys[5] ending in "— Skill" on a row rendered as Lillia is the clearest possible signal the sides drifted from the text.
audit.corrected: Rows 0/2/4/5/6 -> Mel/Lillia/Skill/Skill/Mel in both layers, ratings 3/6/5/5/3. phases[0].why, phases[4].why and phases[6].why rewritten to stop boasting on rows Lillia does not win.
sources: brief whys[0], whys[2], whys[4], whys[5], whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal is the tracked cooldown of the whole page and is never numbered. It is 38/35/33/29/26s — by a distance the longest basic-ability cooldown in the matchup, and it costs 0 mana at rank 5.
audit.why: 38 seconds is the difference between "wait it out" being a real plan and being a slogan. It is also the reason baiting it once wins the whole wave.
audit.corrected: 38s at rank 1 (and free at rank 5) into dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns; 26s at rank 5 into phases[6].why, whys[6] and spikes[3].text.

edits.before: This is where Mel reclaims the lane. Once she has two items her ranged Q poke out-damages your sustain and her R reflects the exact W-and-E commit you need to kill her, bouncing your burst back at your squishy frame. notes: The full layer refers to Mel as "he/him/his" throughout — tldr, winCon, tradeGood, breakdown.early/mid/wave/trading, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].t, report[0]/[3]/[5] — while the content layer correctly says "her". Same defect as karma and kayle in this slice; it wants one champion-wide pronoun sweep rather than a dozen cosmetic edits per matchup, so I filed none here. Not written for lack of a verified detail: Mel's passive stacks Overwhelm infinitely and Golden Eclipse strikes every stacked target globally at 25000 range regardless of distance, so recalling or leaving the lane does NOT put you out of its reach — that is a genuinely dangerous omission from a page that tells the player to roam, but I could not confirm from the kit whether Overwhelm stacks decay over time, and the advice changes completely depending on the answer. QUESTION FOR USER, lillia vs mel, field content.late / wants.you[2]: both tell the player to leave lane and roam once ahead; do Overwhelm stacks persist long enough that Golden Eclipse can execute her from across the map while roaming, and if so should those two strings carry the warning?
